newsitem.title: GERMANY: Broker sees high 1996 Europe malting barley crop.
newsitem.headline: Broker sees high 1996 Europe malting barley crop.

text.p: European malting barley supply would be ample this year as spring barley areas were expanded and yields showed exceptional rises, said German broker Jochen Mautner on the release of his bi-monthly survey.
The 1996 spring barley area in 11 EU countries, which he classifies as relevant malting barley suppliers, was estimated at 6.03 million hectares after 5.67 million ha in 1995.
The specialist broker put average yields in these countries at 4.38 tonnes per hectare, up from 3.36 tph last year, and volume at 26.41 million tonnes versus last year's 19.07 million.
Some 30-40 percent of the crop may qualify for malting.
Mautner said some 70 percent of the crop had been brought in, with France and Spain complete, but the weather over the next few weeks would decide on the final malting availability.
"The remaining 30 percent are cause for concern...if it rains too hard there may be premature sprouting, which disqualifies barley for malting," he said.
"That's why the figures may still change, especially in eastern Germany."
Mautner added the area rises were due to replantings after a harsh winter, which also caused a two-week delay in the harvest, but markets were surprised by the huge yield rises.
Mautner listed spring barley areas in the 11 countries and average protein contents in those parts of their crops, which were currently earmarked for sales to maltsters.
Not included in the totals were Poland with a 988,000 ha area in 1996 (950,000 in 1995) and the Czech republic with 450,000 ha (370,000).
